items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: You know a lot of good — Sonny Rollins, Duke Ellington stuff, all kinds of things.

ctx.x: You had said some pretty kind words about George Avakian? That he gave you some good career boosts along the way. Or is it mostly just listening to his productions?

Well of course I grew up listening to a lot of the things that he did for Columbia, which is not only the reissues but the Miles Davis and Gil Evans. It was his idea to bring those two together. In fact he says he went to Miles and Miles had done all these quintet records and he said, “now that you’re with Columbia, we want to present you in a different way and like put you in a new direction, and we can get this budget together.” And he said, “why don’t you have somebody write something sort of big band or…

that he did. And he had really been kind of out of it so long and he didn’t have really good feelings about the record business, the way it had been run and the way it was being run. But since that time I mean I have to say he’s gotten back into it. He’s doing a lot of work for CBS-SONY with reissue projects. And then just recently this last June for the JVC festival we co-produced a concert which was this — he managed to find these Louis Armstrong compositions that Louis had never recorded, many of them written…
